questions.prompt:
What exact output does code example 1 in this lesson produce?

value = int('42')
assert value == 42
print(value)
questions.explanation:
LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`value = int('42')` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`assert value == 42` — Checks a developer assumption early; relying on assert alone does not protect user input.
`print(value)` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.
